targets.title: Embed and media cards

definition.markdown:
### A10 — Embed and media cards

- **What it does:** cards can hold a bounded web embed (URL-ref, sandboxed
  iframe) or a media reference — the canvas becomes a place where sources
  can be seen, not only cited.
- **Reference behavior:** Excalidraw `embeddable`/`iframe` element types
  (`types.ts:115-140`); Miro embeds (doc-cited).
- **Landing seam:** new `ResearchCard` kinds in the material record; embeds
  store the URL (never a fetched copy — the kernel's material protocol
  serves bytes only for possessed files); strict sandbox attributes;
  pruning law applies unchanged (`researchMaterial.ts:76-78`).
- **UI harmonisation:** embed chrome is a hairline frame + the existing
  card colour system; no vendor badges.
- **Acceptance:** paste a URL → embed card renders interactively; removing
  the source occurrence prunes the card from every frame and saved view

targets.title: The shared time-axis contract for lane 4 (M4′ World/Places)

definition.markdown:
### T6 — The shared time-axis contract for lane 4 (M4′ World/Places)
**What.** One wire shape both M2′ and M4′ consume — dated events with
uncertainty and provenance on a shared time axis, plus period bands and
the session's time window. Not a new store: a published projection of the
reading the instruments already share.
**Reference.** Chronas: one year cursor drives the map's polity layer
(capture 2026-10-07); `ql.techne/v1` already carries every field needed.
**Shape (all existing contract fields, published as the seam):**
```
techne:time-axis/v1 (projection of a TechneReading — no new truth)
  subject_ref, reading_ref, snapshot_revision   (identity, verbatim)
  events[]: { facet_ref | derived_ref, kind,                 (contract.ts:205-222)
              instant | interval{from,to,precisions}, precision,
              uncertainty?, source_ref?, provenance_selector? (temporalFacets.ts:88) }
  relations[]: { relation_ref|derived, relation, from_ref, to_ref,
                 temporal_facet_ref?, standing?, source_ref? }   (contract.ts:145-158)
  bands[]:   { band_ref, label_verbatim, earliest, latest,       (PeriodO shape, T8)
               source_ref?, note?, editorial_note? }
  window:    { from, to } | null                                  (contract.ts:443)
```
**Seam.** Produced beside `relationFieldState` in
`src/techne/m0m5/timeline/` (pure, node-tested); consumed by the
chronology mount (`researchInstruments.tsx:606-636`) and exposed to the
M4′ surface through the hosted app's existing reading channel
(`host.read`, `TechneCentre.tsx:86`) — lane 4 records this interface
point; lane 2 owns the shape.
**UI-harmonisation.** Both instruments display the same window and the
same event extent; a cursor change in either is a session-window change
(S3), not a local secret.
**Acceptance.** Contract test: the projection validates against
`validateReading` inputs byte-deterministically (same reading → identical
projection, the techneBundle purity law); an integration fixture moves the
window and both projections agree on which events are in scope.

definition.markdown:
- **E02 Scene-as-clip: content vs timeline coordinates.** Adopt the
  strip discipline: a Scene's **content identity** (`scene_ref`) is
  stable under every timeline move; its **timeline facts** (order,
  `duration`, `transition`) are mutable addressable state. Editing acts
  never mutate content to move a clip.
  *Reference behavior:* Blender `Strip` carries `start`/`len` with
  `startofs/endofs` handles and `anim_startofs/endofs` media trim
  separated from content (`DNA_sequence_types.h:360-476`); Kdenlive ids
  "have nothing to do with Melt IDs" — model ids stable under all moves
  (`timelinemodel.hpp:44-46`).
  *Mapping:* `scene_ref` ≈ content id; `scenes[]` order ≈ `start`;
  `duration` ≈ `len`. The Scene's living field is the "media" — it has
  no intrinsic length, so no media-trim handles exist (honest divergence:
  a scene shows its whole content; what trims is when it yields the
  stage).
  *Landing seam:* model-level invariant in `model.ts`/`sceneWorkflow.ts`
  (timeline ops reorder/retime but never touch content fields);
  kernel-side `scene_reorder` already carries `scene_refs` — identity is
  preserved by construction (`expression/types.ts:52`).
  *UI harmonisation:* clip chrome (name, save-state dot) persists across
  moves — visual continuity of identity.
  *Acceptance:* property test — after reorder/retime/split sequences,
  every surviving `scene_ref` maps to a scene whose field/entities

targets.title: Insert vs overwrite move semantics; gaps are still scenes

definition.markdown:
- **E04 Insert vs overwrite move semantics; gaps are still scenes.** The
  array is the ripple law: scenes are contiguous, so "ripple" =
  insert/remove shifting successors, and "overwrite" = replace in place.
  A timed void is authored as a **still scene**, not a null gap — the
  audit's stillness floor made literal in the data model (G2).
  *Reference behavior:* Kdenlive `requestClipMove` with group/ripple
  semantics and ripple resize (`timelinecontroller.h:662-665`);
  Blender's explicit gap removal as a separate act
  (`SEQ_edit.hh:69-80`) — oi.journey's contiguous array is the honest
  simplification (a scene is always "there"), so gap tools are not
  ported; instead a **slate/still scene starter** exists.
  *Mapping:* insert = `scene_create` + `scene_reorder`; overwrite =
  `scene_remove` + `scene_create` composite; still scene = `scene_create`
  with a quiet presentation (low count, no automation — authoring starter,
  not a new kind).
  *Landing seam:* `reorderScene` (`app.ts:468`) generalises to the two
  move modes; scene-add menu gains the still-scene starter.
  *UI harmonisation:* drag affordance shows insert edge (line) vs
  overwrite (highlight) — same visual grammar as the entity drag ghost.
  *Acceptance:* insert between scenes 2/3 leaves 1-2 **A** 3-4 →
  1-2-A-3-4 with durations summing identically (receipt: `scene_reorder`

targets.title: Labelled undo/redo converging with kernel act history

definition.markdown:
- **E15 Labelled undo/redo converging with kernel act history.** Undo
  stops being anonymous full-document clones (`store.ts:7-18`, cap 60,
  no labels): each undo entry carries the operation name and the kernel
  changes it produced; undo/redo at or above the last kernel save
  re-issues **compensating kernel changes** (the same grammar, inverted)
  so the kernel revision history and the editor's undo stack describe
  the same work.
  *Reference behavior:* Kdenlive's design law — every elementary change
  writes its own inverse as it executes; composites get undo/redo pairs
  for free and a failing step cancels what was done
  (`timelinemodel.hpp:49-52`); Shotcut's named QUndoCommands
  (`MoveClipCommand` `timelinecommands.h:319`, `SplitCommand` `:484`).
  *Mapping:* the kernel side already receipts: `edit` carries
  `expected_revision` and returns the new revision
  (`kernelExpressions.ts:244-247`); durable act records exist
  (`oi.expression-act/v1`, `expression_act_store.rs:1-33` — replayable,
  archived, never deleted). The editor attaches the change list to each
  undo entry and, when the document is kernel-hosted, derives the
  compensating change set from it (parameter_set for value flips,
  scene_reorder for moves, and so on — the grammar is invertible for
  everything the app emits after E20).
  *Landing seam:* `store.ts` entries gain `{label, changes?}`; save
  path (`kernelExpressions.ts:238-249`) records which entries are
  kernel-clean.
  *UI harmonisation:* undo labels appear in the existing undo affordance
  (and toast on revert), phrased in the app's own voice ("Trim scene 3",
  "Reorder scenes").

  digest equals the pre-edit digest (receipted round-trip); the undo
  stack shows human labels; an act record for the edit is inspectable
  by ref (receipt evidence).

  `store.ts:12-18`) — the target extends it to kernel batches: a

  half-composite.

  path may split one gesture across revisions.

  existing toast/refusal grammar.

  happy path produces exactly one revision increment per gesture.

definition.markdown:
- **E17 Autosave schedule attaining the A1 shape.** Keep the working
  draft safety net, but adopt the schedule the Obsidian A1 study
  costed and the cradle accepted as precedent: trailing-debounce
  autosave, **immediate save on context switches** (scene change, panel
  close, open/save commands), and **flush-on-quit with grace**
  (recreation-backlog T2, `recreation-backlog.md:46-55`; the D-1 posture
  discipline, `:13-21`). Today's 350 ms single debounce (`app.ts:144`)
  plus the 5 s library throttle (`app.ts:159`) becomes: draft debounce
  (unchanged 350 ms coalescing), immediate draft flush on
  `setScene`/rail switch/studio close/beforeunload.

  immediate on command/leaf-switch + flush-on-quit with grace —
  measured, gate-proven classes (recreation-backlog T2).

  (`recovery.ts:55-56` native-first, IndexedDB, localStorage fallback
  order preserved; never a silent browser fallback after native failure
  — `kernelExpressions.ts:71-81` law kept).

targets.title: Atomic, per-document storage; corruption quarantine

definition.markdown:
- **E18 Atomic, per-document storage; corruption quarantine.** The
  standalone library stops being one JSON array written wholesale on
  every save (`store.ts:34` — O(library) per write, one torn write loses
  the library): per-document keys + a manifest, each write atomic
  (IndexedDB keys are atomic; the localStorage fallback mirrors the same
  per-key shape). Unreadable entries are **quarantined verbatim, never
  dropped** — the existing law (`store.ts:29-33`) kept and per-key.
  *Reference behavior:* the kernel's own store discipline
  (`expression_act_store.rs:7-12`: atomic replace = temp + fsync +
  rename, CAS revisions); Shotcut's dedicated autosave-file object
  (`AutoSaveFile : public QFile`, `autosavefile.h:27`).
  *Mapping:* **D-1 decision point, restated for this lane** — Obsidian
  writes in place, non-atomic; the D-1 posture chose atomic-by-default
  with a documented divergence note, chosen once and never mixed
  (`recreation-backlog.md:13-21`). This target adopts that posture:
  atomic per-document writes, divergence note "no single-file vault
  compatibility to preserve" (the library is app-local, not an
  interchange format).
  *Landing seam:* `store.ts` (library) + `recovery.ts` draft stores;
  migration: existing array library read once, split per-document, array
  retained read-only one release, then quarantined.
  *UI harmonisation:* none; failure voice unchanged ("Existing library
  could not be read. It has not been overwritten.").
  *Acceptance:* corrupt one document key → others load, the bad key is
  listed in `readLibraryDetailed().errors` and preserved byte-verbatim
  (existing contract, now per-key); torn-write simulation (partial
  write) never loses a *different* document.

definition.markdown:
### T5. Transitions are authored per-edge objects, not one implicit crossfade

**What it does:** each ordered pair of scenes carries an authored
transition: time (seconds), curve, and switch semantics
(immediate / sync / at-end — a transition may wait for the outgoing
scene's natural end). Authored on the strip or beat surface, persisted
inside the scene-material envelope alongside `duration`/`transition`
(the envelope already holds per-scene entry-transition seconds;
this generalises it to the *pair* semantics Godot models).

**Reference behavior attained:** Godot's
`AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition`: `xfade_time`, `xfade_curve`
(`Ref<Curve>`), `SwitchMode {IMMEDIATE, SYNC, AT_END}`,
`break_loop_at_end` (`animation_node_state_machine.h:37-63`). Today the
journey has exactly one mechanism — a preview-only canvas crossfade with
`transitionEasing` hardcoded `'linear'` (`app.ts:301-302`) — against the
app's own UX-contract admission: "The preview's page dissolve is not a
physical transition law" (`docs/UX_CONTRACT.md:45`).

**Landing seam:** transition authoring state joins the scene-material
presentation envelope (`scene_material_set`); runtime blending consumes
lane-3's transition-capable engine. **Consumes lane-3: transition-capable
engine** (§Dependency 1).

**UI harmonisation:** the transition editor uses the shared inspector
form grammar (the strip's existing duration/transition inputs are its
seed); curves render in the engine's own easing-curve visual language.

with each edge honouring its time/curve/switch mode; at-end edges hold
the outgoing scene to its natural end; reload restores the authored
edges from the kernel document (envelope round trip). Confidence: high on
the persistence seam (pattern proven by `oi.journey-scene/v1`), medium on

targets.title: Overlap-to-blend authoring: dragging scenes into overlap authors the transition

definition.markdown:
### T6. Overlap-to-blend authoring: dragging scenes into overlap authors the transition

**What it does:** on the strip, dragging a scene to overlap its
neighbour's tail authors/extends the transition between them; the overlap
width *is* the transition duration; separating the scenes to zero overlap
returns to a cut.

**Reference behavior attained:** Unity Timeline's blend model, verbatim:
"In a blend, the first clip is referred to as the outgoing clip and the
second clip is referred to as the incoming clip. The area where the
outgoing clip transitions to the incoming clip is referred to as the
blend area. The blend area sets the duration of the transition."
(`clp_blend.html`, verified verbatim 2026-10-07 — documentation-only
possession, RE-TARGETS.md §2.C).

**Landing seam:** the strip's existing drag machinery
(`app.ts:766-768` → `reorderScene`); overlap state writes the same
per-edge transition state as T5.

**UI harmonisation:** drop-target and snap visuals follow lane-3's snap
model (their Kdenlive RE basis) so drag feels identical on strip and
timeline; **Consumes lane-3: per-scene save/restore UX + snap grammar**
(§Dependency 4).

**Acceptance shape:** drag scene B's head over scene A's tail by N px →
the pair's transition reads N seconds; playing the join shows one blend
of that duration; screenshot pair before/after shows the strip rendering
the blend area (render-verified, not self-reported).

**What it does:** the journey surface persists its position and local

targets.title: Semantic saving: the kernel Expression stays the only store of record

definition.markdown:
### T20. Semantic saving: the kernel Expression stays the only store of record

**What it does:** everything durable about journeys and palaces saves as
`oi.expression/v1` state through the kernel's CAS-gated edit: scene order
(`scene_reorder`), scenes (`scene_create`/`scene_remove`), scene material
including duration and per-edge transitions (`scene_material_set`,
`oi.journey-scene/v1` envelope), whole-journey presentation
(`oi.journey-properties/v1`), palace region Scenes with their one-member
bodies, portal triggers and guided order. Every proposal carries the
snapshot revision (`expected_revision`); a `revision_conflict` is refused
loudly with the draft preserved; replay of an applied composition emits
nothing (idempotence by diffing against the live snapshot).

**Reference behavior attained:** the kernel's own operation guard — one
edit carries at most 256 changes against a 2048-object bound
(`kernelComposition.ts:138-147`) — and Godot's resource discipline:
transitions are `Resource`s saved with the state machine, never a side
file. Lane 3's Kdenlive RE basis (request-functions with their own
inverse) is the operation-architecture this already matches.

**Landing seam:** `kernelComposition.ts` / `composition.ts` as they
stand — the target binds every new surface (T1–T19) to these two
composition floors, no third write path.

**UI harmonisation:** save/receipt feedback uses the app's existing
markSaved/toast channels; conflict handling shows the preserved-draft
state in the notice grammar.

**Acceptance shape:** save under a stale revision → loud
`revision_conflict`, draft intact, nothing partially written; replay the
same composition twice → second save is a no-op ("Nothing to save",
`palaceInstrument.tsx:151-152` already proves the pattern); reopened
kernel document reproduces scenes, order, bodies, triggers and material
(readback-verified, the palace Save's existing double-check).

boot can open from it, so two sources of journeys coexist silently. The

until first saved to the kernel; library entries record their origin

silent coexistence; no deletion of local work.

silent truth; Twine's library is explicitly a *local* library with
publishing as a separate act.

the kernel boot path decides precedence.

masthead/library list grammar).

library entry marked local; open a kernel Expression → library entry

rehome_tickets.what: Technē's Record ("Record walk", shell/modeGrammar.ts) waits for the journey owner: once it stands, bind Record to capture the atlas's camera waypoints with their holds and captions — presentation, never a dated-place claim or a minted route — as a walk the owner keeps, replayed on the atlas's one time button (Technē's Walk). Homes lane-4 T25; a subject's thread already walks.

rehome_tickets.title: M3′ Journey binds a walk's stop to its beat
rehome_tickets.what: Binding a stop to a Journey beat is M3′ Journey's (lane O's judgement; M4′ renders nothing journey-owned): once G5 records walks, let the Journey lens bind a stop to a beat by ref, under the material's own law (fsj/src/placeTourRecord.ts resolveTourBindings: a deleted beat leaves the stop intact and unbound). Homes lane-4 T26.

rehome_basis.law: A target counts as implemented only when its home is reachable in the candidate and reads its real owner (FOUNDATION §8). Homes are read from the code (each path:line re-opened against its quote) and held to candidate-reachable.mjs; the person's path to each home is code-read; the screen leg is the lead's.

reprogress_basis.law: An implemented claim stands only on evidence that still holds at a named revision: its commits in history, each source quote in its file (the line re-pointed, never the quote), each described source file and each test file present. A row with no source or test citation left, or a named gap, returns to pending with a dated note naming what vanished and where its behaviour went. Commit evidence alone never keeps implemented. exercised, passed, failed and blocked are untouched.
